title: Still On When It Gets There

scenes.tts: A neuron hears its survival signal at the far end of its axon. How does the message get home?
scenes.visual: Title card: Still On When It Gets There. A sympathetic neuron: cell body at left, a very long axon with a break marker, terminals in an organ at right. Label: not to scale.
scenes.narration: A neuron hears its survival signal at the far end of its axon. How does the message get home?

scenes.tts: A sympathetic neuron collects N G F at axon terminals that can sit centimetres from its cell body.
scenes.caption: A sympathetic neuron collects NGF at axon terminals that can sit centimetres from its cell body.
scenes.visual: NGF dots gather at the terminals. A scale bar along the axon: centimetres.
scenes.narration: A sympathetic neuron collects NGF at axon terminals that can sit centimetres from its cell body.

scenes.tts: The terminal hears the factor. But the nucleus decides whether the cell lives.
scenes.visual: The nucleus glows, with a live or die switch beside it.
scenes.narration: The terminal hears the factor. But the nucleus decides whether the cell lives.

scenes.tts: In these young neurons, dying needs new genes switched on in the nucleus. So a survival signal from the tip has to be able to act on the cell body.
scenes.visual: Scope label: young sympathetic neurons, NGF at the axon tips. Genes in the nucleus light up. An arrow points from the terminal toward the cell body, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: In these young neurons, dying needs new genes switched on in the nucleus. So a survival signal from the tip has to be able to act on the cell body.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry through. A target keeps a neuron alive only if its signal makes the trip home.
scenes.visual: On screen: A target keeps a neuron alive only if its signal makes the trip home and is able to signal when it gets there.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry through. A target keeps a neuron alive only if its signal makes the trip home.

scenes.tts: And it must be able to signal when it gets there. On when it arrives, not necessarily on every second of the trip. Binding at the tip is not enough.
scenes.visual: Binding at the tip is crossed out as the test; an active signal arriving at the cell body is ticked.
scenes.narration: And it must be able to signal when it gets there. On when it arrives, not necessarily on every second of the trip. Binding at the tip is not enough.

scenes.tts: So could the signal simply drift home, by diffusion?
scenes.visual: A single glowing molecule at the terminal, starting a random walk.
scenes.narration: So could the signal simply drift home, by diffusion?

scenes.tts: Diffusion time grows with the square of the distance.
scenes.visual: On screen: time ≈ (distance)² / (2 × D). D, the diffusion coefficient: about 10 square micrometres per second for a soluble protein.
scenes.narration: Diffusion time grows with the square of the distance.

scenes.tts: For a typical soluble protein and an axon one centimetre long, how long would the trip take?
scenes.visual: The axon labelled 1 cm = 10,000 micrometres. A clock with a question mark.
scenes.narration: For a typical soluble protein and an axon one centimetre long, how long would the trip take?

scenes.tts: Roughly two months. Over a few centimetres, many months.
scenes.visual: On screen: 10,000² / 20 ≈ 5 million seconds ≈ two months. A calendar flips through eight weeks.
scenes.narration: Roughly two months. Over a few centimetres, many months.

scenes.tts: Worse, many signals are proteins carrying a phosphate. Enzymes called phosphatases keep removing it.
scenes.visual: Zoom inset with a scale bar: a protein with a glowing phosphate tag; a phosphatase snips it off and the glow goes out.
scenes.narration: Worse, many signals are proteins carrying a phosphate. Enzymes called phosphatases keep removing it.

scenes.tts: Suppose a phosphate lasts about ten seconds.
scenes.visual: On screen: a phosphate lasts about 10 seconds. Illustrative rate.
scenes.narration: Suppose a phosphate lasts about ten seconds.

scenes.tts: Then the active signal falls to about a third every ten micrometres from the tip.
scenes.visual: A cloud of glowing signal spreads from the tip and fades smoothly, with a thinning tail, along the scale bar. Label: fade distance about 10 micrometres; illustrative rates.
scenes.narration: Then the active signal falls to about a third every ten micrometres from the tip.

scenes.tts: A centimetre is a thousand of those steps. The rates are illustrative, but the conclusion holds.
scenes.visual: Zoom out: the faded cloud is a speck at the tip of a 1 cm axon. Label: 1 cm = 1,000 fade distances. Illustrative rates, not TrkA measurements.
scenes.narration: A centimetre is a thousand of those steps. The rates are illustrative, but the conclusion holds.

scenes.tts: It does not arrive late. It arrives switched off.
scenes.visual: Grey, switched-off molecules drift toward the cell body; no lit signal arrives.
scenes.narration: It does not arrive late. It arrives switched off.

scenes.tts: So the signal needs a vehicle or a relay. And it must be able to signal when it arrives.
scenes.visual: Checklist: 1, able to signal when it arrives (needed). 2, the target's message kept distinct from other signals along the way (helpful, not shown to be required).
scenes.narration: So the signal needs a vehicle or a relay. And it must be able to signal when it arrives.

scenes.tts: One candidate fits both needs. At the tip, N G F binds its receptor, Track A.
scenes.caption: One candidate fits both needs. At the tip, NGF binds its receptor, TrkA.
scenes.visual: NGF dimer binds two TrkA receptors at the terminal membrane.
scenes.narration: One candidate fits both needs. At the tip, NGF binds its receptor, TrkA.

scenes.tts: Ligand and active receptor are pulled into the cell together, in a vesicle called the signaling endosome. It can keep signaling while carried.
scenes.visual: The membrane pinches in around NGF on TrkA, forming a vesicle. Label: signaling endosome. NGF sits inside the vesicle; the TrkA kinase tails stick out into the surrounding cytoplasm, where they can signal.
scenes.narration: Ligand and active receptor are pulled into the cell together, in a vesicle called the signaling endosome. It can keep signaling while carried.

scenes.tts: The motor protein dynein drags it along microtubules toward the cell body.
scenes.visual: Dynein walks the endosome along a microtubule toward the cell body.
scenes.narration: The motor protein dynein drags it along microtubules toward the cell body.

scenes.tts: At roughly a micrometre each second, a centimetre takes a few hours.
scenes.visual: On screen: about 1 micrometre per second; 1 cm in about 3 hours.
scenes.narration: At roughly a micrometre each second, a centimetre takes a few hours.

scenes.tts: So what arrives must still be able to signal, after hours on the way. Carrying alone is not enough.
scenes.visual: Three endosomes set off; one loses its glow within minutes, one dims, one is still bright at the cell body. Label: illustrative lifetimes.
scenes.narration: So what arrives must still be able to signal, after hours on the way. Carrying alone is not enough.

scenes.tts: This model is favoured. But is it proven? Hold that question.
scenes.visual: Label: favoured, not proven. A question mark stays on screen.
scenes.narration: This model is favoured. But is it proven? Hold that question.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: a survival signal must make it home still able to signal.
scenes.visual: Closing card: on when it gets there, able to signal.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: a survival signal must make it home still able to signal.
